summary: Halcyon Cognitive Systems is evaluating Redwood Dedicated to host real-time customer assistants and regulatory monitors. Primary negotiation is around guaranteed minimum throughput (tokens/sec), concurrency caps, and burst policies that align with trading-hour spikes. They require VPC deployment, KMS integration, SOC2 compliance, and US data residency. Procurement prefers an annual reserved contract with SLA acceptance tests and service credits tied to deterministic runbook outcomes.
throughput_requirements: Target steady-state minimum: 60,000 tokens/sec (cluster-level) — business-critical for chat and reranking pipelines.
Concurrency cap requirement: support 200 concurrent long sessions (avg 256 tokens/response) without degrading p95 beyond agreed SLO.
Burst policy: tolerate bursts up to 220,000 tokens/sec for up to 2 minutes (trading open/close), with automatic throttling fallback beyond burst window.
Scaling tolerance: prefer reserved baseline + transparent burst pool (pay-as-you-burst) rather than opaque preemption of other customers.
latency_and_slos: p50 < 70ms (text-gen requests, short mesosize prompts), p95 < 250ms for conversational flows (with KV-cache warm).
Availability target: 99.95% monthly for dedicated capacity; request credit formula for missed uptime and per-incident latency breaches.
Tail-latency runbook requested: root cause analysis timeline, escalation path, and compensated credits if SLO not met for >2 consecutive hours.
reserved_gpu_planning: Current PoC config: 4x H100 equiv — marginal on throughput; SE recommends 8x H100 (preferred) or 12x A100-80 as committed baseline.
Reservation ask: committed GPU pool with headroom for 25% peak headroom; explicit billing for reserved units and separate burst billing.
Placement: region us-east-1 only, single-tenant scheduling preferred for deterministic performance.
sla_negotiation_points: Minimum guarantees: define tokens/sec guarantee at cluster and per-customer slice levels; include test harness and acceptance criteria.
Credits: linear credit schedule for missed availability and defined credits for repeated latency SLO violations (not purely discretionary).
Burst handling: explicit burst pool sizing, preemption policy (no silent preemption of reserved workloads during burst usage), and transparent throttling behavior.
Maintenance windows: max 4 hours/month for disruptive maintenance; Redwood to notify 72 hours in advance for non-emergency windows.
Operational runbooks: Redwood to provide playbooks for capacity incidents, and SLA teleconference within 30 minutes of incident classification.
poC_notes_and_results: PoC objective: verify 60k tokens/sec steady across chat+rerank mix and meet latency SLOs at 200 concurrent sessions.
Result: 52k tokens/sec run at current 4x H100 equiv; p95 at 320ms under sustained load — below target.
Action: SE recommended reserved bump to 8x H100 and enabling prefix/KV cache optimizations plus batching tweaks in Redwood Optimize.
Acceptance test plan: three consecutive 1-hour runs meeting steady-state throughput and latency thresholds during business hours (9-11am), followed by legal signoff.
